professionalService.problemSolved: Explains a proposed construction sequence for one hillside house through an aligned programme, staged 3D site and fixed-week drawings.
professionalService.serviceOutcome: The visitor sees excavation through structure, props, finishes and handover while a week indicator and programme move together, then the completed house returns to drawing 06 on the six-view sheet.
professionalService.decisionValue: Useful for discussing intended construction order and temporary works only as an illustration. The 38-week durations and stage assignments are authored demo content, not a calculated schedule or actual execution record.

evidence.statement: Three-viewport forward captures traverse site and return to six drawings.

qaExpectations.invariant: Weeks, phases and actual progress are labeled according to their authoritative source; authored illustration is not reported as execution.
Element IDs and geometry remain stable as temporal appearance and removal are evaluated.
Props, formwork and staging appear and disappear at sourced intervals without changing permanent model identity.
Six or fewer independent time views do not contaminate one another through shared uniforms, materials, depth or camera state.
Forward, seek and reverse produce the same state for the same absolute time.
Reverse restores the programme dock, captions, camera and rendering as well as scroll origin.
Programme and call to action do not overlap at 390×844; 844×390 retains legible programme and site.
Any exported sheet uses current project geometry and labels its time/source.
Presentation never writes donor phase assumptions or geometry into the saved Rubik project.
